invariants_checked: All seven evaluation calculators (BLEU, ROUGE, NDCG, MAP, MRR, Precision, Recall) handle nil MetricInput, empty/duplicate retrieval sets, and zero denominators without panicking or emitting NaN/Inf scores.
NDCGMetric rejects non-positive cutoffs (k <= 0) before slicing RetrievalIDs, and deduplicates repeated retrieved document IDs while preserving rank discounts.

Smoothed BLEU returns 0 when candidate or reference ground truth has zero lexical tokens, rejects negative/NaN/Inf weights, avoids log.Fatal in phrase serialization, and ROUGE normalizes metric/stat selectors while reconstructing LCS iteratively without call-stack recursion.

findings.summary: NDCGMetric.Compute panicked on negative k cutoffs (ids[:n.k]), smoothed BLEUMetric returned 0.5-0.84 against empty/punctuation-only ground-truth references and called log.Fatal in phrase.String(), RougeMetric panicked with a nil-function dereference on unknown/uppercase metric names and used O(N+M) stack recursion in reconLcs, and all seven metric calculators dereferenced nil MetricInput without guarding.

invariants_checked: Cron and one-shot triggers validate timezones via embedded time/tzdata, forbid CRON_TZ=/TZ= expression overrides, preserve sub-second RFC3339Nano instants across normalization, and enforce DefaultMinInterval across upcoming firing gaps.

RenderInstruction substitutes placeholders in a single strings.NewReplacer pass (preventing second-pass placeholder injection from AutomationName/RunID), and RunQuery truncates carried prior results strictly on UTF-8 rune boundaries.
Lifecycle.Begin registers activity before invoking start and rolls back registration on both returned errors and recovered panics so per-kind concurrency caps never leak.
Lifecycle.Finish writes the completion notice before removing live registration and emits work_finished only on the winning first Push.

Listeners snapshots registered SessionLifecycleListeners under RWMutex, ignores nil registrations, recovers per-listener panics in NotifyStop/NotifyDelete/NotifyDeleteAborted so remaining listeners still execute, and preserves shared registry/inbox state when any OnDelete listener fails or panics.

findings.summary: Lifecycle.Begin leaked the registered ActivityRegistry slot if the start callback panicked, and Listeners accepted nil registrations and allowed a single panicking listener to abort remaining session stop/delete cleanup hooks.

invariants_checked: RunActivityRegistryContract and RunNoticeInboxContract verify per-session isolation, cross-tenant isolation across identical SessionIDs (TenantsAreIsolated), per-kind concurrency caps under goroutine contention, lease renewal/expiry, first-push idempotency, retention pruning, and race-free Ack/Clear semantics.
RedisTLSConfig enforces TLS 1.2+ with certificate verification enabled by default unless REDIS_TLS_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY=true.

TruncateUTF8Bytes and CleanInvalidUTF8 preserve valid UTF-8 boundaries and strip NUL bytes, PipelineLog sanitizes structured log values against log injection and typed-nil Stringers, WithDeadlockRetry honors context cancellation, and DeduplicateWithScore maintains a strict weak ordering even in the presence of NaN scores.

findings.summary: DeduplicateWithScore allowed a first-seen NaN score to shadow valid finite scores for the same key and violated slices.SortFunc strict weak ordering when sorting NaN entries, formatPipelineLogValue panicked on typed-nil fmt.Stringer values (such as (*url.URL)(nil)), and WithDeadlockRetry did not guard nil contexts.

invariants_checked: Cryptographically random 128-bit hex owner tokens guard atomic Lua compare-and-delete (Release) and compare-and-pexpire (Renew) scripts so an expired holder never deletes or extends another holder's lock.

WithRenewableLock separates caller cancellation from OwnershipContext cancellation, enforces 0 < renewInterval < lease and lease >= 1ms, and reports ErrLockOwnershipLost if renewal or release loses ownership.

findings.summary: validateOperation accepted positive sub-millisecond leases (0 < lease < 1ms), causing Renew to pass lease.Milliseconds() == 0 into PEXPIRE and immediately delete the caller's owned lock in Redis while reporting renewed=true.

invariants_checked: NormalizeOrigin and NormalizePattern accept only http/https origins or *.domain[:port] / * patterns without userinfo, paths, queries, fragments, IP wildcards, IPv6 zone IDs, empty/leading-zero/out-of-range ports, trailing/leading/empty DNS labels, or CSP-breaking characters.

Allows enforces exact scheme+host+port matching or strict dot-boundary subdomain matching (preventing evil-example.com suffix tricks and port mismatches), and FrameAncestors fails closed to frame-ancestors 'none' when patterns are empty or invalid.

findings.summary: NormalizeOrigin and NormalizePattern accepted dangling empty-port colons (https://a.example:, *.example.com:), out-of-range/leading-zero ports (:0, :65536, :0443), leading/consecutive/trailing FQDN dots (*..example.com, *.example.com.), IPv6 % zone IDs, and unsafe characters (<, >, `), causing FrameAncestors to emit broken CSP tokens (http://*.example.com::*) and Allows to wildcard all ports on *.example.com:.

invariants_checked: Load honors explicit ENV_FILE across all builds, restricts implicit dotenv loading strictly to .env.lite on Lite builds (executable directory first, then CWD), ignores stray .env files, and never overwrites existing process environment variables.
All HTTP/application ErrorCode constants, parse-stage wire codes, and session sentinel errors preserve stable numeric/string values and generic anti-enumeration messages.
IsAppError unwraps %w-wrapped error chains via errors.As while rejecting nil and typed-nil *AppError pointers, and (*AppError).Error() is nil-receiver safe.

findings.summary: IsAppError used a direct err.(*AppError) type assertion instead of errors.As, missing %w-wrapped AppErrors and returning (nil, true) on typed-nil *AppError values, while (*AppError).Error() panicked on a nil receiver.

invariants_checked: Serve always closes reader on every path (including HEAD and 416 Range errors), sets X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, strips Unix/Windows path components and control characters from Content-Disposition filenames, and forces attachment + application/octet-stream whenever active browser content (.svg, .html, .xml, .js, etc. or active MIME types) is served without Download: true.

findings.summary: Serve used platform-specific filepath.Base in Content-Disposition (leaking Windows backslash traversal segments on Linux and emitting filename="/" or ".." on degenerate inputs) and allowed caller-supplied active ContentType values (text/html, image/svg+xml, text/javascript) to override SafeContentTypeByFilename when Download was false.

invariants_checked: In-process anydoc conversions enforce empty-input rejection, normalize format extensions consistently, drop WithAssets on PDF inputs, classify typed resource_limit failures permanently via ErrResourceLimit without re-parsing hostile inputs, cap AST block/inline walk depth, and report ErrUnavailable cleanly when built without -tags anydoc.

findings.summary: backendConvert unconditionally retried ToMarkdownBytes after ToDocumentWithAssetLinks hit a permanent resource_limit rejection (parsing hostile XML/ZIP bombs twice), Convert compared opts.Format == "pdf" without normalizeExt normalization, and AST block/inline walkers lacked a recursion depth guard.

invariants_checked: Compound header validation verifies the 8-byte OLE2 signature, 512/4096 sector shifts, and header sector counts before mscfb allocation, returning ErrUnsupported on non-OLE2 inputs.

validateOLEStreamChain verifies DIFAT, Directory, FAT, and MiniFAT chains for cycles and unallocated/special sector markers before reading Workbook/Book streams, and readStream bounds both initial buffer capacity (64 KiB) and total stream bytes (256 MiB and verified chain capacity) regardless of forged streamSize or caller fileSize.

BIFF5/BIFF8 record parsing bounds SST allocations/iterations, skips overlapping BoundSheet substreams to prevent quadratic re-parsing, enforces worksheet row/col grid limits, and recovers panics as errors.

findings.summary: mscfb stream reads lacked FAT/MiniFAT cycle and special-sector validation (allowing cyclic FAT[0]=0 chains to synthesize repeated workbook sectors up to declared stream size), readStream preallocated min(f.Size, fileSize) upfront before reading bytes, checkCompoundHeader omitted the 8-byte OLE2 magic check (failing to return ErrUnsupported on >=512B non-OLE2 files with 0x0009 at offset 30), and parseSST looped over raw uint32 unique counts.

invariants_checked: HTTP and headless Chromium fetches enforce SSRF validation on initial URLs, redirect hops, DNS-pinned dials, and local Chromium HTTP/CONNECT proxy requests, blocking loopback, RFC1918, CGNAT, link-local metadata, IPv4-in-IPv6 translations, restricted ports, userinfo credentials, and FQDN trailing-dot internal hostnames.

Chromium child processes run with a strict minimal environment allowlist (blanking parent secrets and LD_*/DYLD_* variables), bounded global concurrency semaphore, <-loopback> proxy enforcement, Host-header normalization on HTTP proxy requests, and bounded response/DOM body sizes.

findings.summary: chromiumSSRFProxy and Fetcher.pinnedDialContext/resolvePinnedTarget did not canonicalize FQDN trailing dots (allowing http://localhost./, http://metadata.google.internal./, and .corp. to bypass hostname suffix checks), pinnedDialContext omitted restricted-port checks before DNS resolution, Fetch and resolvePinnedTarget accepted userinfo credentials in URLs, and chromiumSSRFProxy.handleHTTP did not pin outReq.Host to outReq.URL.Host.

invariants_checked: Classify fails closed (Invalid) on nil or malformed net.IP slices and categorizes loopback, RFC1918, IPv6 ULA (fc00::/7), site-local (fec0::/10), link-local (169.254.0.0/16, fe80::/10), CGNAT (100.64.0.0/10), 0.0.0.0/8, 240.0.0.0/4, RFC 2544/6890 reserved, RFC 6666 discard-only (100::/64), TEST-NET documentation, IPv4-mapped (::ffff:0:0/96), RFC 2765 SIIT IPv4-translated (::ffff:0:0:0/96), 6to4 (2002::/16), Teredo (2001::/32), NAT64 (64:ff9b::/96, 64:ff9b:1::/48), and IPv4-compatible (::a.b.c.d) addresses.

findings.summary: classifyIPv6 and embeddedIPv4 omitted RFC 2765 SIIT IPv4-translated addresses (::ffff:0:a.b.c.d, e.g. ::ffff:0:169.254.169.254 and ::ffff:0:127.0.0.1) and RFC 6666 discard-only IPv6 addresses (100::/64), misclassifying them as Public.

invariants_checked: MarkServerStarted, ServerStartedAt, ServerUptime, SilenceGinRouteSpam, and LogGinRouteCount synchronize global state via atomic.Pointer without data races.

LogStartupEnv redacts sensitive secrets to character lengths only, warns on invalid SYSTEM_AES_KEY lengths, missing HMAC signing keys, and insecure Redis TLS, and sanitizes non-sensitive env values against CR/LF log injection.
ShutdownBudgets splits total grace periods into positive HTTP drain and resource cleanup budgets summing to total.

findings.summary: MarkServerStarted/ServerStartedAt/ServerUptime read and wrote a non-atomic package-level time.Time struct and SilenceGinRouteSpam/LogGinRouteCount shared a non-atomic *int64 pointer (triggering -race data races under concurrent access), and formatEnvValue logged non-sensitive environment variables without stripping CR/LF log-injection characters.

invariants_checked: Align indexes normalized unit keys in a single linear pass, preserves numeric signs/decimals/inequalities, rejects unaccounted TOC/duplicate occurrences, and never attributes unmapped gaps to adjacent pages/blocks.

Office/EPUB structure extractors enforce per-entry (64 MiB, verified on actual decompressed stream rather than declared ZIP header alone) and cumulative per-archive (128 MiB) decompression budgets across docx, pptx, xlsx (via excelize UnzipSizeLimit/UnzipXMLSizeLimit), and epub, while rejecting ../ archive root escapes.
Index.Locators clamps out-of-range offsets safely without slice bounds panics and marks chunks containing unmapped text as Partial.

findings.summary: epubUnits and pptxUnits lacked a cumulative archive decompression budget (allowing repeated spine/slide references to a single compressed member to amplify memory without hitting maxUnits), xlsxUnits called excelize.OpenReader without UnzipSizeLimit/UnzipXMLSizeLimit, readZipFile silently truncated entries spoofing UncompressedSize64, resolvePart allowed ../ traversal and epubUnits failed on leading-slash rootfiles, and Index.Locators did not re-check end <= start after clamping.

invariants_checked: AllowedMap, AllowedList, FirstAllowed, and IsAllowed normalize delimiters and casing against the closed 8-provider canonical list (local, minio, cos, tos, s3, oss, ks3, obs), returning defensive copies and ignoring unknown provider tokens.

RedisNoticeInbox namespaces keys by both TenantID and SessionID, writes notices with atomic HSETNX+PEXPIRE Lua scripts, and deletes expired notices via compare-and-HDEL Lua scripts so concurrently re-pushed IDs survive.

MemoryStreamManager and RedisStreamManager clamp negative fromOffset values to 0, clone StreamEvent structs/Data maps to prevent caller-slice/map data races, use millisecond PEXPIRE/PExpire TTLs so sub-second TTLs never truncate to 0s key deletion, bound initial Redis Ping timeouts while closing failed clients, and guard LiveRun transitions with SetNX and CAS Lua scripts.

findings.summary: RedisNoticeInbox.key omitted SessionRef.TenantID from the Redis hash key (fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s:bg-inbox", prefix, SessionID)), allowing sessions sharing a SessionID across different tenants to read, collide with, acknowledge, or clear each other's background completion notices.

GetEvents and GetSteerEvents panicked on negative fromOffset in MemoryStreamManager (slice bounds out of range) and queried tail elements with negative nextOffset in RedisStreamManager; AppendSteerEvents mutated caller slice Timestamps in place (racing on shared slices) and truncated sub-second Redis TTLs to EXPIRE 0 (immediately deleting the steer list); and NewRedisStreamManager leaked Redis client pools on Ping failure.

invariants_checked: ToSimplified uses immutable post-init dictionaries with bounded <=10-rune greedy phrase-then-character matching, verified concurrent-safe and bit-identical against the 13,177-entry SHA-256 historical FAQ corpus.
